extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, patentees and practitioners handling Indian patent matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the Indian Patents Act, Patent Rules and Examiner Guidelines covering restoration/surrender, Controller powers, appeals, infringement, confidentiality, penalties and patentability evaluation (particularly for chemicals, pharmaceuticals and biotechnology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed patents – statutory conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent has ceased to have effect under Section 53(2) because of non-payment of renewal fees, the patent and any specified patent of addition thereto may be restored provided that the application is made without undue delay, and within eighteen months from the date on which it has ceased, and that the failure to pay the renewal fee was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eighteen months reckoned from date of cessation; any extension for payment should be considered. Application must be on Form 15 with supporting evidence. Any patent of addition to be restored should be specified. Separate Form 15 is required for each main patent; no fee payable for patent of addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for restoration / procedural prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee or his legal representative should make the application; where two or more persons held the patent jointly, with the Controller’s leave one or some only of them may apply without joining the others. Assignee may apply only when assignment has been registered; if patent granted to a deceased person action under Section 44 should be completed before restoration is begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patentee failed to register a change of name before cessation he must first apply (Rule 94) to correct the register; if changed name after cessation must prove identity and draw/sign application in new name with 'formerly known as' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and evidence required in restoration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include a statement fully setting out the circumstances that led to the failure to pay the renewal fee. This statement may be supported by evidence and copies of any documents referred to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must be of a recent date to show absence of undue delay. Evidence may cover several patents. Evidence must support claim that failure to pay was unintentional and that there has been no undue delay. Controller may call for further evidence (letters, deeds etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentionality – limits and illustrative principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim that the failure to pay was 'unintentional' is examined strictly: deliberate election not to pay under an erroneous supposition is not 'unintentional' (Land's Patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration is confined to the patentee's last decision before expiry of the extended time for paying renewal fee under Section 53(2); previous changes of mind are irrelevant. Any post-cessation decision not to apply for restoration is fatal. Financial inconvenience is not a ground, but destitution causing physical impossibility may be considered. Negligence by an agent may not suffice unless proved; proved negligence in agent’s office may be sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's initial prima facie assessment and hearing opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If Controller does not consider a prima facie case for restoration made out, the applicant is notified; unless applicant states within one month that he desires to be heard the application may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has one month to request to be heard after notification of lack of prima facie case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to restoration – who, timing and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person interested may give Notice of opposition to the application within two months of appearance of the advertisement in the Official Gazette. Grounds under Section 61(1): (a) that the failure to pay was not unintentional; and/or (b) that there has been undue delay in making the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be made on Form 14 in duplicate with a statement of opponent's interest, grounds and facts relied on. Controller sends copy to applicant. Procedure in rules 57–63 (filing written statement, reply, evidence, hearing) applies, as far as may be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for restoration and protection of intervening users
rubrics_metrics.description: If decision is favourable and applicant pays unpaid renewal fees within one month and specified additional fee, patent is restored and Controller advertises accordingly (Rule 86).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every order for restoration should include provision under section 62(1) to protect persons who began using the invention between lapse and advertisement. Controller may impose other conditions for protection and compensation. No suit or proceeding for infringement shall be commenced/prosecuted in respect of an infringement committed between lapse and date of advertisement of restoration application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from restoration decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee or opponent may file an appeal to the Appellate Board from any decision of the Controller made under Section 60 within three months from the date of the decision or within further time the Appellate Board may allow under Sections 117A(2) and 117A(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be in prescribed form with copy of decision and prescribed fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of patents – procedure and opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may offer to surrender his patent at any time; Controller advertises the offer and informs persons shown in register as having interest. Three months opposition period from advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition in Form 14 (duplicate) within 3 months with prescribed fee. Hearing procedure similar to opposition to grant (rules 36–45). If Controller accepts offer, he may direct the patentee to return the patent and will revoke upon receipt; revocation occurs only after receipt of physical patent. Orders under section 63 are appealable to High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and roll of scientific advisers (Rule 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller should maintain a roll of scientific advisers for purposes of Section 115; Rule 103(2) prescribes qualifications for enrolment. Provision exists for removal of names from the roll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Section 115 does not statutorily oblige courts to choose advisers from the roll, in practice courts find it convenient to select from the roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's civil-court-like powers (Section 77) – summons and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller empowered to summon and enforce attendance of any person and examine him on oath, akin to Order 16 CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of several civil-court powers listed (see separate entries for discovery, affidavits, commissions, costs, review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's power to order discovery/interrogatories and obtain documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may administer interrogatories to opponent to obtain admissions in writing; Controller can direct and obtain documents relied upon to prove alleged facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery by interrogatories is a means of shortening litigation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's power to receive evidence on affidavits and oral evidence (Order 19 applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller empowered to receive evidence on affidavits (Order 19 CPC applies) and may take oral evidence in lieu of or in addition to affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 19 rules apply except to extent inconsistent with Rule 126 of Patent Rules. Controller may allow cross-examination on affidavits and accept documentary evidence unaccompanied by affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's power to issue commissions for examination (Order 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller empowered to issue Commissions for examination of witnesses or documents where persons are exempted from personal appearance per Order 26 CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where witnesses cannot appear in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's power to award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: In all proceedings before the Controller, he has discretion to award costs which are reasonable having regard to all circumstances of the case; awarding costs is subject to the Fourth Schedule of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may award compensatory costs in any proceeding considered false or vexatious; guided by Order 35 CPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and setting aside of Controller orders (forms and time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller can be requested to review his decision by filing Form 24 with prescribed fee within one month of communication of decision; one-month extension allowable if request filed before expiry of first month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convincing grounds (e.g., new evidence) should accompany Form 24; review governed by Order 47 CPC (Rules 2,4,7,9). Ex parte orders may be set aside under Order 9, Rules 13–14 by filing Form 24 within one month; extension of one month allowed by filing Form 4 with fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's power to correct clerical errors (Section 78)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller may correct any clerical error in any patent, specification document or matter entered in register either suo moto or on request by a person interested upon filing prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Suo moto, Controller shall give notice to concerned persons and opportunity to be heard. If requested correction may alter meaning/scope, Controller shall advertise in official journal. Correction power is without prejudice to sections 57 and 59—cannot use correction as a guise to amend specification; if correction amounts to amendment, follow section 57 procedure and satisfy section 59. Interested person may oppose amendment by Form 14; Controller proceeds as under sections 25 & 26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's powers in taking evidence (Section 79)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order 19 CPC dealing with affidavits is applicable except where inconsistent with Rule 126. Controller may take oral evidence instead of or in addition to affidavit evidence and allow cross-examination on affidavit contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may accept documentary evidence without accompanying affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of discretionary powers and extension of time (Section 80, Rule 138)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before exercising discretion adversely to any applicant for patent or amendment, Controller should give party opportunity to be heard within prescribed period if requested at least 10 days before expiry of the respective time limit. Controller empowered to extend time for acts under various provisions (e.g., Rule 138).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While extending time Controller not required to give notice or opportunity to interested parties; no appeal lies from orders granting such extension (Section 81, Rule 138).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action against infringement – pre-suit steps and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee should inform in writing alleged infringer that patent rights are being infringed; parties may settle (licensing, arbitration). If settlement fails, patentee may sue. Limitation governed by Section 40 of Indian Limitation Act: three years from date of infringing act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cause of action arises where infringing act occurred; suit filed in district court having jurisdiction. If defendant counterclaims for revocation, suit and counterclaim transfer to High Court. Suit maintainable even if revocation petition pending before another court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of burden of proof in process-product cases (Section 104A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where patent subject-matter is a process to obtain a new product and there is sufficient likelihood that identical product is made by patented process and patentee cannot, despite reasonable efforts, determine the process used by the alleged infringer, court may direct defendant to prove that his process is different, provided patentee first proves product is identical to product directly obtained by patented process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court shall not require disclosure of manufacturing/commercial secrets if unreasonable to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolar (regulatory) exception and parallel import (Section 107A)
rubrics_metrics.description: India provides Bolar provision under S.107A(a): allows generic manufacturers to use patented inventions to obtain marketing approval from public health authorities without patent owner's permission before patent expiry. Parallel import under S.107A(b): importation of patented products by any person authorized by the Patentee will not be considered infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables early regulatory testing and importation from licensee abroad without permission of patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate Board – constitution, jurisdiction and appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellate Board established under S.83 of Trade Marks Act, 1999 is appellate board for Controller decisions (S.116) to speed proceedings; consists of Chairman, Technical Members and staff. Appeals to Board must be in prescribed form with copy of decision and fees within three months or such further time as Board may allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals available in respect of many Controller decisions (list includes S.17,18,19,20,25,28,51,54,57,60,61,63,66,69(3),78,84,85,88,91,92,94). Certain orders (e.g., Central Govt orders re defence inventions, Controller secrecy directions under Section 35, revocations under S.65/S.66) are not appealable. No appeal from Controller granting extension of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of pending proceedings to Appellate Board (Section 117G)
rubrics_metrics.description: S.117G provides Appellate Board is sole authority; appeals and revocation cases pending before High Court shall be transferred to Appellate Board from notified date. Board may proceed from beginning or from transferred stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central Government will notify the date from which transfers occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction upon publication of specification (Section 143)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent and any specification filed will not be published or open to public inspection except with applicant's consent, before eighteen months from date of application or priority date or before being open to public inspection under section 11(3) or 43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to secrecy provisions for certain inventions in Chapter VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information relating to patents – access and fees (S.153 & Rule 134)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information relating to patent applications or patents can be obtained from Controller by making request in prescribed manner subject to payment of prescribed fee (Rs.300 for natural person and Rs.1200 for legal entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature of information obtainable specified in Rule 134 of Patent Rules, 2003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of examination reports (Section 144)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of examiners to the Controller will not be open to public inspection or published and are not liable to production or inspection in legal proceedings unless court certifies production is desirable in interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects internal examiner reports unless court orders otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reports of patent office to Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report regarding patent applications filed in India and processing of such applications and execution of the Act will be placed before Parliament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate patent procedure (Section 154, Rule 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent is lost or destroyed, a sealed duplicate may be obtained by making request in prescribed manner and on payment of prescribed fee; procedure is under Rule 132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies admissible as evidence (Section 147 & Rule 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of any entry in any register or of any document kept in the patent office or of any patent, purporting to be certified by Controller and sealed, shall be admitted in evidence in all courts and proceedings without further proof or production of original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller or patent office officer not compellable to produce the register or document where contents can be proved by certified copy unless court orders for special causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may call for information on working of patent (Section 146)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller has power to call for periodical statements as to extent to which patented invention has been commercially worked in India; patentee or licensee must furnish such information within two months of notice or such further time as Controller allows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supply information is an offence punishable under Section 122. Patentees/licensees should furnish annual statements (Form 27) within 3 months of year end per Rule 131. Controller may publish information received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security for costs where parties not resident or carrying business in India (Section 150)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any party giving notice of opposition or applying for a licence neither resides nor carries on business in India, Controller may require security for costs and may treat opposition/application as abandoned if security not given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent binds Government (Section 156)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall have for all intents and purposes the same effect as against Government as it has against any person, subject to other provisions of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of security of India (Section 157A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Central Government may not disclose information relating to any patentable invention/application which it considers prejudicial to security of India and may take action including revocation in interest of security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section parallels provisions in sections 35–38 and 40–42; 'security of India' meaning includes fissionable materials, traffic in arms/ammunition, and actions in time of war or emergency in international relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for contraventions (Sections 118–124)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various offences with penalties: (a) contravention of secrecy provisions S.118 – imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both; (b) falsification of register entries S.119 – imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both; (c) unauthorized claim that article is patented S.120 – fine up to Rs.100,000; (d) wrongful use of words 'patent office' S.121 – imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both; (e) refusal/failure to supply information S.122 – fine up to Rs.1,000,000 (and imprisonment up to 6 months if false info knowingly); (f) practice by non-registered patent agents S.123 – fines for first and subsequent offences; (g) offences by companies S.124 – company and responsible persons deemed guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts of some fines not specified in statute text; Section 122 also applies where central government undertakings using patented invention for government must furnish info under S.100(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination guidelines – scope and aim (Annexure I introduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines aim to help Examiners examine patent applications in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, chemicals and biotechnology (isomers, polymorphs, pro-drugs, active metabolites, hydrates etc.) given public health, techno-economic and industrial significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in applications may include new drug molecules, pharmaceutical preparations, synergistic combinations, combination of new chemical entity with known component, agrochemicals, new chemical products, new products via biotechnological/microbiological/biochemical processes, microorganisms, products from natural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key aspects to assess for product patents in chemicals/pharma/biotech
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant aspects for grant of product patents: deciding appropriate prior art; assessment of novelty of claimed product/process; determination of inventive step; criteria for industrial applicability; unity of invention; sufficiency of disclosure and scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify for a patent, inventor must show novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), industrial applicability and that invention does not fall under non-patentable categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of isomers
rubrics_metrics.description: Isomers (structural/positional and stereoisomers) are different compounds with same molecular formula. Structural isomers may be novel over prior art even if similar; stereoisomers are prima facie obvious—once racemate is known its enantiomers are obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural isomers showing close structural and functional similarity may still be novel but may be obvious if enabling methods are available. Stereo isomers: product patent may not be granted for enantiomers of a known racemate; however, when a new compound is claimed for first time in optically active pure form, a product patent may be granted (examples and case law indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of homologues
rubrics_metrics.description: Homologues normally display add-on property and are structurally similar and may lack inventive step; examination must be case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art need not be true homologs to render claimed compounds prima facie obvious if structural and property similarity is close (case examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of polymorphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymorphic forms (different crystal forms) can be deemed within the prior art and therefore not patentable as products; however, a new polymorph prepared by a novel process involving inventive step may allow a process patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapeutically active ingredients in polymorphic forms with differing properties may be unpatentable if inevitably obtained by prior art process or covered by a previous product patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of metabolites
rubrics_metrics.description: Metabolites are compounds formed inside a living body during metabolism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A metabolite is unpatentable since administering the drug to a patient naturally and inevitably results in formation of that metabolite.
